source.title: How to decay your learning rate

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including supplementary material; some flattened tables and figure text are difficult to associate, but relevant training-error statements are explicit.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether learning-rate schedules affect training error in CIFAR settings and reports that easy CIFAR tasks reach zero training error with simple schedules before weight-norm bouncing, so schedules make no difference. It also reports nonzero training error after 200 epochs with data augmentation.
record.gate_note: Reports training-error results for Wide ResNet CIFAR experiments with and without data augmentation, directly bearing on V1. Other schedule comparisons that report only test performance do not bear on the claim’s training-error outcome. Weight-norm and initialization plots are not results about reaching near-zero training classification error except where explicitly described alongside performance.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own training classification errors for Wide ResNet models on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 under different schedules and augmentation settings, directly bearing on V1.
record.authors_conclusion: The record captures the easy-task qualification but understates the main conclusion. The authors find that weight-norm bouncing appears necessary, but insufficient, for complex schedules to outperform a constant rate followed by one late decay. ABEL uses weight-norm dynamics to match tuned schedules with greater hyperparameter robustness. Easy tasks that reach zero training error before bouncing show no schedule advantage.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies schedule effects and weight-norm dynamics, not the cited original studies’ primary interventions. Its CIFAR results use Wide ResNet models and vary learning-rate schedule and data augmentation.
record.method_sensitivity: Training-error outcome differs with data augmentation; zero training error is reported without augmentation, while with augmentation it is not reached after 200 epochs.

fits_no_version.finding: Very small initialization scales degrade final test performance and eliminate weight-norm bouncing in WRN 28-10.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization scale affects generalization and weight-norm dynamics in batch-normalized residual networks; these measurements do not establish V4's training-speed or trainable-depth effects.

fits_no_version.finding: ABEL adapts to large initial learning rates by reducing them rapidly and can converge where other schedules fail.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adaptive learning-rate decay improves tolerance of large initial rates; this does not establish recovery above a measured stability threshold as specified by V5.

record.problems: Most experiments use one initialization; the paper says CIFAR Wide ResNet experiments in Table 1 use three seeds, but reports no uncertainty for the training-error statements in Supplementary B.4. The with-augmentation result is described textually without an exact training-error value.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant training-error results left out. Schedule comparisons in Tables 1 and 2 report test metrics, not training classification error; weight-norm-only plots do not qualify as rows for V1.

untested.parts: Random or corrupted labels, Adam training on CIFAR, model-size dependence, and substantial residual error under smaller models or other regularized recipes. The augmented experiments do not establish whether final error exceeds near-zero.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious local minima, and additional student neurons.
Depth-dependent training degradation and comparisons with identity shortcuts.
Activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient propagation, training speed, trainable depth, and orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization.
Initial linearized stability thresholds, curvature changes, loss recovery above those thresholds, and full-batch edge-of-stability dynamics.
Controlled comparisons of training speed or learning-rate tolerance with and without batch normalization, including Fixup.

missing.what: Both simple and cosine schedules reach zero training error after only 15 epochs on CIFAR-10 without augmentation.
missing.locator: Figure 4b caption; Supplementary B.4 and Figure S4g–i

record.verdict_notes: The augmented result warrants no limits_scope verdict: nonzero error alone cannot distinguish near-zero error from substantial error. Weight-norm bouncing is distinct from the curvature and loss dynamics named in V5. This study is not an original source listed for any version.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test random or corrupted labels, Adam, smaller models, or the broader range of model sizes and early-stopping or regularized recipes in the version.
